name: OPA111 / OPA2111
type: Difet JFET-input low-noise precision op-amp, 1/2 ch
tagline: Burr-Brown's low-noise Difet with pA bias, 'the popular OPA111' to TI. Japanese rollers prize the metal-can OPA2111AM.

lineage.note: Created the Difet OPA111 and OPA2111. Last BB datasheets PDS-526K (1995), PDS-540E (1993); macromodels 1990.
Re-issued as SBOS138 / SBOS140. OPA2111 NRND, KP obsolete, OPA111 gone. No second source.

part_numbers.note: Single; datasheet SBOS138 (PDS-526K). TI E2E: 'no longer available'; suggests OPA196.
TO-99 can, NOS. EWB: AM 100 µV/0.8 pA, BM 50 µV/0.5 pA.
Probably military-temperature metal can; SMQ probably hi-rel screened (unconfirmed).
Dual; SBOS140 (PDS-540E). TI Japan reportedly 'in discontinuation'. Blog quotes 1.5 µVpp 0.1–10 Hz.
TO-99 cans; AM is prized. EWB Ib: AM/SM 2, BM 1.2, KM 3 pA.
8-pin plastic DIP; NOS. Broker bought at €18, resold €35 (2023). Sold as 'Audio Grade'.

key_specs.value: 8 nV/√Hz max at 10 kHz; 30 nV/√Hz at 10 Hz (BM)
250 µV, 1 µV/°C max (OPA111); AOL 120 dB, CMRR 100 dB min
OPA111 1 pA max; OPA2111 4 pA max

reputation.summary: A niche cult part among vintage rollers and a known pA-bias instrumentation front end. Japanese blogs praise the metal-can OPA2111AM as warm and analog; one swap from OPA827 gave clearer vocals and wider soundstage. A Zigsow reviewer found the plastic KP harder than OPA2134. Soomal says OPA627/637 resolve treble far better. No ASR or Samuel Groner measurements.
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in headphone amps (JP/CN hobbyists)
DC servo in low-noise physics preamps
caveats: Discontinued; supply is NOS or broker stock, so remarks are a risk.
Slow by modern standards (about 2 MHz, 2 V/µs).
TO-99 cans need lead forming or an adapter for DIP-8 sockets.
AM vs KP sound differences are grade/package plus folklore; no die change documented.
Soomal's descriptors are for Difet parts as a class; Iq and output drive unconfirmed.

counterfeit_notes: No documented fakes; NOS supply and cult prices invite remarks. Check BB logo, pre-2000 date code, marking (M = TO-99, P = DIP). Bias should be low-pA, not nA; slew far above 2 V/µs suggests an NE5532/TL07x remark.

silicon_changes.summary: OPA2111 was discontinued after about 26 years; OPA111AM/BM are also obsolete (date unknown). No die or fab PCN found. RFAB PCNs 20220328001.1 and 20210811000.1A were not shown to include these parts.
silicon_changes.identification: Lifecycle only: DigiKey lists OPA2111KP and AM obsolete; Octopart lists OPA111AM/BM obsolete.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None to the silicon; parts sold now are old broker stock or possibly counterfeit.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: discontinuance only; no same-part-number silicon change.
silicon_changes.verification: E2E EOL thread, DigiKey and Octopart status confirmed. No PDN number or exact date found.

refuted_claims: OPA2111KU (SOIC) removed: model list is AM/BM/KM/SM (TO-99) and KP (DIP); no KU found.
'No TI literature number for OPA2111' is wrong: it is SBOS140 (PDS-540E, Oct 1993).
AM vs KP 'package-era split' is not a silicon hazard: no die change evidence, only grade/package and one review.
corrections: OPA111 datasheet identified: SBOS138 = PDS-526K, August 1995.
OPA2111 datasheet identified: SBOS140 = PDS-540E, October 1993; SBOS140 added.
8 nV/√Hz is a 100%-tested maximum at 10 kHz for both parts.
Added headline maxima: OPA111 1 pA, 250 µV, 1 µV/°C, 120 dB, 100 dB; OPA2111 4 pA.
Status: OPA2111 NRND, OPA2111KP obsolete, OPA111 no longer available.
Added OPA111SMQ and the OPA196 alternative.
Added many mirrors and the 1986/1989 BB IC Data Books as older-revision sources.
